**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep dispatch runs out of required check contexts**

Because this workflow exposes `workflow_dispatch` using the same three job names proposed as required status contexts, a manual run for the relevant commit can publish successful GitHub Actions checks without genuine PR H/B/S binding. `capture_context` accepts `workflow_dispatch`, while `require_pr_acceptance` is never called by these jobs, so the commands still exit successfully and the report is marked `PASS`. Put diagnostic dispatches under distinct, non-required job names or make these required jobs non-successful for dispatch events.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind normalized reviews to their captured pages**

These checks only require the assembled review submissions and thread captures to have the expected top-level JSON type; they never derive or compare them with the separately inventoried pagination responses. A candidate can therefore replace `final-review-submissions.json` with even `[]` (or erase the thread data), update the acquisition-index and manifest hashes, and still pass `validate_evidence`, causing the archive gate to certify incomplete review evidence. Reconstruct or cross-check these normalized files against every declared captured page.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate run-log ZIP contents before accepting job evidence**

When evidence uses the run-level `RUN_ID-logs.zip` produced by `acquire`, this branch treats mere file existence as proof that every expected job has a log. An empty, corrupt, or incomplete ZIP can be entered into the acquisition index and manifest with repaired hashes and will satisfy all jobs in that run—including both Application contract jobs—without being opened or matched to job IDs. Parse the bounded ZIP and require a nonempty log member for each job before accepting it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject job-level permission overrides**

This only verifies that the workflow contains one read-only top-level `permissions` block, but GitHub Actions permits a job-level `permissions` mapping to override it. A later PR can add `permissions: {contents: write}` to any candidate-executing integrity job and `validate_workflow` still returns success, defeating the contract intended to keep the token read-only. Reject every job-level override or parse the workflow and verify the effective permissions of each job.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject backgrounded verifier commands**

The shell-token blacklist omits a single `&`, so a required command can be changed to `python ... & true` while still matching its expected prefix and passing `validate_workflow`. In that scenario the step reports the status of `true` rather than the verifier, allowing a failed or unfinished integrity check to publish a successful required job. Reject asynchronous shell operators as well, or validate that each run entry is exactly the expected argument vector.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind local verification to checkout HEAD**

When a local operator supplies a stale but reachable SHA—especially to the one-time `maintenance_scope` acceptance command—this branch returns a valid `local` context without comparing the candidate to `rev-parse HEAD`. The verifier can therefore emit PASS for a previous synthetic merge or ancestor after the checkout has advanced, so the local preflight does not establish that the tested candidate is the current checkout; perform the same candidate-to-HEAD check used in the CI branch before accepting a local context.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the offline guide in the tooling closure**

When `archival/v0.2.0/README.md` is changed after packaging without refreshing the supplement's `OFFLINE_REPRODUCTION.md`, the archive gate still passes because the expected closure scans only `verification/integrity` and `verification/archive`. The builder explicitly snapshots the canonical guide, but the verifier never compares that snapshot with the current guide, so standalone reproduction instructions can silently become stale while the tooling-closure check reports success; include the guide in the checked closure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the fixed comments to their captured content**

If either archived comment body is replaced with arbitrary nonempty text and the acquisition-index and manifest hashes are repaired, `validate_evidence` still accepts the archive because it checks only the comment ID, issue URL, and nonemptiness. This allows the final exact-head review statement or the acceptance receipt containing H/B/S/M and workflow identities to be erased while the archive gate reports PASS; pin the expected author, timestamps, and body digest or validate the required source and acceptance fields.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Point the tooling source commit at an ancestor**

In the candidate-bound `archive-reproducibility` workflow, this manifest pins tooling commit `507ff2461762a248b6a5f90dc966d11627c4b1b9`, but the reviewed commit `f03a3d4ce1c924102fdbe5375a26b16a239935b1` has sole parent `37c0cb8f2fbe7934639127e5f8b6d64a01e6950f`, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 507ff24 f03a3d4` returns false. Because `validate_tooling` unconditionally requires the manifest's tooling commit to be an ancestor of the candidate, the required archive job will fail before restoration for this commit and its PR synthetic merge; rebuild the supplement using a tooling commit reachable from the candidate or preserve this tooling commit in the candidate's ancestry.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

This ancestry failure does not reproduce on the actual PR objects. The live head is H=171c954c4733d2c8eaaac3ad90e60e4d1d4637c3, base B=37c0cb8f2fbe7934639127e5f8b6d64a01e6950f, and genuine synthetic S=7743ecbcfec71711f6be9a035934ac01a767c40d with ordered parents [B,H]. Both `git merge-base --is-ancestor 507ff2461762a248b6a5f90dc966d11627c4b1b9 H` and the same command against S return 0. The cited f03a3d4ce1c924102fdbe5375a26b16a239935b1 is neither actual H nor S; I make no claim about the origin of that different object.

The fresh isolated [archive job](https://github.com/HMarcusWH/PermanssonLean/actions/runs/39066296586/job/117494574237) also passed the actual T→S ancestor check and reports source_candidate=S, source_commit=T, binding=canonical_T_C_and_executing_code. The production ancestor requirement remains intact. Integration will use a merge commit preserving H/T ancestry; a future rebase or squash that removes T requires rebuilding the tooling snapshot. The other three findings in this review remain open and are being fixed separately.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove dispatch-capable jobs from required contexts**

When this proposed ruleset is activated, the newly required legacy contexts can still be satisfied by manual runs: `.github/workflows/lean.yml`, `research-lean.yml`, `verification.yml`, and `application.yml` all expose `workflow_dispatch` under the same `build`, `research`, `executable-verification`, and two Application context names listed here, and none performs genuine-PR H/B/S binding. Thus a dispatch on the relevant PR head can publish successful required checks without exercising the PR merge context; use separate diagnostic job names or reject dispatch in every required context.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the committed publication ZIP**

The archive job validates only `archival/v0.2.0/supplement-1`; a repository-wide search found no check that reads the new `publication-candidate/Permansson_v0.2.0_archival-supplement-1.zip` or its checksum. Because that path is also outside the preservation policy's closed roots, a later change can corrupt or stale the actual publication candidate and update its checksum while every proposed required job still passes, despite the publication README claiming that the ZIP exactly packages the supplement. Add a required comparison of the ZIP's safe member inventory and bytes against the verified supplement.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound the delivered file inventory**

When verifying an untrusted standalone supplement, `scan_files` walks, hashes, and retains a record for every delivered file before `validate_manifest` can reject extra paths, but it enforces neither a file-count limit nor an aggregate-byte limit. An input containing a very large number of empty or individually valid-size extra files can therefore consume unbounded traversal time and memory inside the offline parser instead of reaching the intended bounded rejection; stop once the fixed object/file-count and aggregate closure budgets are exceeded.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
